public_rationale: The October selloff is material evidence to consider when testing the trigger, but it does not establish a broad AI-investment collapse. Microsoft's September-quarter results cannot establish how most big-tech companies fare after such an event. The antecedent therefore remains unknown, requiring a conditional scoring hold.
limitations: A different interpretation of bubble bursts could classify the October selloff differently.
Even under that interpretation, the cited earnings period precedes the selloff and cannot settle the aftermath.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: When the bubble bursts, the vast majority of big tech will be fine, at least in the short term.
conditions: at least in the short term

statement.excerpt: And, most crucially, the vast majority of big tech will be fine, at least in the short term, when the bubble bursts.

from_speaker: the vast majority of big tech
at least in the short term
our_interpretation: The antecedent is a broad collapse of the AI investment boom. A market selloff is relevant evidence but does not automatically establish that event.
Big tech is anchored by the surrounding references to the Magnificent Seven and specifically Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon and NVIDIA.
Fine means remaining financially viable and continuing ordinary operations. The context expressly permits large valuation declines and impairments.
Vast majority means a clear large majority, without inventing an exact percentage.
Short term refers to the immediate reporting periods after an established collapse. The speaker supplies no fixed duration.
criteria.support_condition: After a documented broad AI-bubble collapse, a clear large majority of the relevant major technology companies remain solvent, maintain adequate liquidity and continue ordinary operations during the immediate aftermath.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the same documented trigger, financial failures, emergency rescues or severe operational disruption affect enough major technology companies that a clear large majority cannot be described as financially viable.
